_note: Gas turbine and heat-recovery steam generator of US 5,366,514 FIG. I (patent items 37 and 27) for plantagent/combustion.py. Tags GT-201 / HRSG-201 are ours (the PlantAgent P&ID stops at the VRC loop). Every value names its source; ILLUSTRATIVE marks values the patent does not give.

composition_mol.source: ILLUSTRATIVE: typical US pipeline natural gas; the patent gives no fuel analysis

fuel.heating_value_basis_source: ASSUMPTION: gas-turbine fuel input is conventionally quoted on LHV; the patent does not state the basis

fuel_MMBtu_h.source: US 5,366,514 Table I: natural gas to combustion gas turbine (CGT) 112.28 MMBtu/hr, 80 F, 600 psig

shaft_kW.source: DWSIM K-201 shaft power of the solved model (the turbine drives the vapour compressor only, patent col. 7)

exhaust_T_C.source: ILLUSTRATIVE: typical exhaust temperature of the Solar Mars-class industrial turbine the patent names; vendor performance data not on record

loss_pct.source: ILLUSTRATIVE: gearbox, bearing and casing losses of the fuel input

steam_lb_h.source: US 5,366,514 Table I line 32: high-pressure steam 35,000 lb/h

feedwater_T_C.source: US 5,366,514: HRSG feed from the condensate storage tank (col. 7); Table I line 24 condensate 180 F (approx)

economizer_approach_K.source: ILLUSTRATIVE: design economiser approach to saturation

casing_loss_pct.source: ILLUSTRATIVE: HRSG casing/radiation loss of the gas-side duty

ua_gas_exponent.source: typical practice for off-design HRSG rating: gas-side-controlled UA scales with gas flow^0.6 (e.g. Ganapathy, Waste Heat Boiler Deskbook)

min_pinch_K.source: typical practice: evaporator pinch not below about 8 K

min_economizer_approach_K.source: typical practice: economiser approach at least about 5 K to avoid steaming

stack_dew_margin_K.source: typical practice: keep a non-condensing stack above the water dew point with a margin

installed.source: US 5,366,514 describes an unfired HRSG (no supplementary firing)

residence_s.source: ILLUSTRATIVE: residence time at the local flame temperature for the thermal-NO screening

min_O2_wet_pct.source: typical practice: duct burners need roughly 11 % O2 or more in the turbine exhaust for stable firing
